solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hunt encourages tax cut for fellow MPs as before

indicators.note: a word that is cut is trimmed short, losing its tail end

blocks.note: to comb an area is to search or hunt through it
urges on, spurs
an old word for a tax or assessment

explanation.surface: A huntsman urging hounds on and cutting the tax burden for fellow members of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: SESS (also CESS) is an archaic tax; cut, it loses its last letter. 'As before' flags the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A comburgess was an old term for a fellow burgess, a borough's representative elected to sit in Parliament.

clue.text: Parts of jellyfish sometimes seen caught with time at sea

indicators.note: being at sea is being confused and all over the place, so the word before is jumbled

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
T is the standard abbreviation for time
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bits of a jellyfish occasionally spotted, caught in time while out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sometimes' belongs to the definition: ctenes are the comb plates of comb jellies, which are only loosely called jellyfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ctenes are the comb-like swimming plates of ctenophores, creatures commonly but loosely lumped in with jellyfish.

clue.text: Staple food one accepted in the borders of Mbale?

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its two outside letters, first and last
the pieces before are placed inside the edge letters that follow

blocks.note: Mbale is a town in eastern Uganda; its first and last letters are kept
A as the indefinite article means one
took means accepted, as in took the offer

explanation.surface: Asks what everyday food a person might take up in a Ugandan border town.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the hint that this food belongs in Uganda, where Mbale is.
explanation.definitionFit: Matooke is the cooking banana, steamed and mashed, that forms the basic daily diet across much of Uganda.

clue.text: Odd bits of Briton’s story

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are the bits kept

blocks.note: letters one, three and five of Briton

explanation.surface: Fragments of a British person's life tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A bio is a short biography, the written account or story of someone's life.

clue.text: No big building complex open

indicators.note: 'no big' asks for the three letters of the word big to be taken out of what follows
something complex is intricate and tangled, so the remaining letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be removed
taken as written, the word they come out of

explanation.surface: A development with no large building in it is open to the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing B, I and G from BUILDING leaves ULDIN, which rearranges to UNLID.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlid something is to take its lid off, uncovering it and so opening it up.

clue.text: Doctor raking in high earnings gets a small snack

indicators.note: a person raking in money gathers it into their keeping, so one piece holds the other
high here means intoxicated, so the word it describes is in a muddled state

blocks.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-paid physician celebrates a big salary with a modest bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the anagram verb, but it is the outer piece; 'high' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingersnap is a crisp ginger biscuit, the kind of thing nibbled as a light bite between meals.

clue.text: Trots, say, struggled with noble’s domain in Poland

indicators.note: letters that have struggled are thrashing about, so they land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Trotskyists struggling against a Polish aristocrat's estate, as revolutionaries might.
explanation.walkthrough: Trots is slang for Trotskyists; 'say' is just more letters, not a sound hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A starosty was the estate or district held by a starosta, a Polish nobleman granted crown land.

clue.text: Rudeness lost customers

indicators.note: letters that are lost have strayed from their places and must be put back in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop's impolite staff drove away its clientele.
explanation.definitionFit: End users are the people who finally buy and use a product, a company's ultimate buyers.

clue.text: Pickled onion’s first consumed after seconds

indicators.note: the first means only the opening letter of the word it follows
after puts the following abbreviation in front of the rest

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for seconds
the opening letter of onion
consumed as in used up

explanation.surface: A pickled onion eaten quickly after the first one, with seconds taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickled' is both a hint at onions and the definition: soused also means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To souse food is to steep it in vinegar or brine, so soused herring or onions are preserved in that way.

clue.text: Shower dividing Labour producing material that smears

indicators.note: something dividing a word splits it apart by sitting in its middle

blocks.note: labour as hard work
a shower of rain

explanation.surface: A political storm splitting the Labour Party produces mudslinging.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour with a capital looks like the party, but it simply means hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Train oil is greasy oil rendered from whale blubber, a substance that leaves smears on whatever it touches.

clue.text: Middle Eastern capital picked up lots of gossip

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upward

blocks.note: Sana, or Sana'a, is the capital of Yemen

explanation.surface: A city in the Middle East absorbed plenty of rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts a sound-alike reading, but in a down clue it means lifted upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ana is a collection of anecdotes and table talk about a person, so several of them make plenty of tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Former Liberal coming round to praise highly

indicators.note: the pair coming round the next word surround it on both sides

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A one-time Liberal politician finally comes round to singing someone's praises.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or glorify enthusiastically, heaping admiration on someone.

clue.text: Opposed to opening Iceland briefly? Leads to complaint

blocks.note: anti means against
an adit is a horizontal entrance into a mine
IS is the international code for Iceland

explanation.surface: Someone against Iceland's frozen-food store opening nearby, with a grumble resulting.
explanation.walkthrough: Iceland is both the country and a British frozen-food shop chain, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiaditis is an old medical name for tonsillitis, an illness and so a complaint in the medical sense.

clue.text: Navy worker you heard getting the bird

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound, a single letter that is spoken the same

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for Navy
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
the letter name is pronounced like the pronoun

explanation.surface: A sailor told off and given the bird, that is, jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the bird' suggests being booed; the bird here is a real one.
explanation.definitionFit: The nhandu is the South American rhea, a large flightless ratite resembling a small ostrich.

clue.text: No good eating fried onion for midday meal break

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside itself
fried food is cooked and broken down, so these letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: NG is the abbreviation for no good
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Eating fried onion is a bad idea for a lunch break.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooning is a dialect or American term for a rest and meal taken at noon, a lunch hour.

clue.text: Hesitation not fully shown around river boats

indicators.note: a word not fully shown is missing its final letter
the shortened word goes around the next abbreviation, enclosing it

blocks.note: a pause is a hesitation
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Hesitation over a river crossing, with the boats only partly in view.
explanation.definitionFit: A prau, or proa, is a fast Malay sailing vessel, so praus are a kind of craft.

clue.text: Reporting again in prison

indicators.note: in means the first piece sits inside the second

blocks.note: a cage confines like a prison
over as in do it over, once more

explanation.surface: A journalist reporting from jail for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: News coverage is the reporting given to an event by the press and broadcasters.

clue.text: Rattle pondered getting slower and softer

indicators.note: to rattle something is to shake it about, so the following word is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Sir Simon Rattle, the conductor, considered a slower and quieter tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor, which makes the musical setting natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdendo is an Italian musical direction meaning dying away, decreasing in both tempo and volume.

clue.text: A lot of drink for group of friends

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a posset is a hot drink of milk curdled with wine or ale

explanation.surface: Plenty of alcohol for a gang of mates.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a posse is one's crew or gang, the circle of friends one hangs about with.

clue.text: No power mentioned for feudal district

indicators.note: no power means its abbreviation is dropped from the word

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power
mentioned as in spoken of

explanation.surface: A powerless feudal territory referred to in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mentioned' looks like a sound signal, but it is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A soken was a district under a lord's jurisdiction in medieval England, a feudal territory or soke.

clue.text: Independent is carrying leader on Rupert Murdoch

indicators.note: the leader of a name is its first letter
carrying means holding the next piece within

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for Independent
the opening letter of Rupert
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Independent newspaper carrying a story on media mogul Rupert Murdoch.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Murdoch looks like one name, but the definition is Murdoch alone: the novelist Iris Murdoch.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch was the Irish-born British novelist and philosopher, author of The Sea, the Sea.

clue.text: Extremely strict girl cracking joke

indicators.note: something cracking another breaks into it and ends up inside

blocks.note: a pun is a joke on words
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A very severe girl finally laughing at a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritan as an adjective describes rigid, austere moral standards and disapproval of pleasure.

clue.text: Sour liquid accepted on a recipe?

blocks.note: A is a dictionary abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill
the on side in cricket is also the leg side
taken as written
R, from Latin recipe meaning take, heads a prescription

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sour drink was okayed because a recipe called for it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Alegar is vinegar made from soured ale, the malt counterpart of wine vinegar.

clue.text: Head outside Italy for normal drowned valleys

indicators.note: the first word sits outside the next abbreviation, wrapping it

blocks.note: a ras is a headland or cape
I is the international code for Italy

explanation.surface: A boss stationed outside Italy in place of the usual one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Normal' qualifies the definition: these are ordinary drowned river valleys, as opposed to glacial fjords.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long narrow inlet formed when the sea floods a river valley, as along Galicia's coast.

clue.text: Disturbance in jet, tense for pilot upfront

indicators.note: for means one letter takes the place of another

blocks.note: a spurt is a jet of liquid
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
the front letter of pilot

explanation.surface: Turbulence on a jet makes the pilot at the front tense.
explanation.walkthrough: Disturbance in jet reads as air turbulence, but disturbance is the definition and in a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturt is an old and dialect word for trouble, commotion or a fuss, a stir.

clue.text: Bond admits going too far for hot stuff

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a tie is a bond or link
OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: James Bond overdoing it with a sexy woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond with a capital suggests 007, but it just means a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Tottie is British slang for attractive women collectively, regarded as sexy, hence hot stuff.

clue.text: Boys saving energy for Guides!

indicators.note: saving something keeps it safe inside

blocks.note: lads are boys
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Boy Scouts conserving their strength for the Girl Guides.
explanation.walkthrough: Guides with a capital and exclamation suggests the girls' movement; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead is to show the way or direct, so leads works as a verb meaning guides.

clue.text: Jovial Londoner, ’es managed West ’Am

blocks.note: first meaning: a cheery cockney, the type named after a dropped-aitch Harry
second meaning: a football manager known by his cockney first name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arry, Harry with the cockney dropped H, was the Victorian name for a lively working-class Londoner; Harry Redknapp managed West Ham, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockney form of Harry names both a stock cheerful London type and the famous football manager Redknapp.

clue.text: Crop that’s novel spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of means the title is said out loud and matched by sound

blocks.note: Emma is a Jane Austen novel; in a non-rhotic accent it ends the same way

explanation.surface: A farm crop that features in a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmer is an ancient variety of wheat, still grown as a cereal crop.

clue.text: Some older referees returning made mistakes

indicators.note: some of the words means only a part of their letters is taken
returning means going back, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A few veteran referees going back on bad decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so erred is the past tense meaning got things wrong.

clue.text: Foot specialist treated my tibias? Not unknown

indicators.note: treated, as by a doctor, means worked on and so rearranged
not unknown means the letter for an unknown quantity is removed

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A chiropodist asked to look at the patient's shin bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot specialist' points to a chiropodist, but the foot here is a metrical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An iambist is a poet who writes in iambs, the metrical foot of one short and one long syllable.

clue.text: Learn about one American nurse, a gem

indicators.note: about means placed round the following pieces

blocks.note: to get something is to learn or grasp it
A as the indefinite article means one
an RN is a registered nurse in the US

explanation.surface: Studying a US nurse who is a real treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnet is a deep red silicate mineral cut and polished as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Second experiment, soprano unused in choral music

indicators.note: unused means left out, so this letter is dropped

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a test is an experiment
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A second trial for a choir in which the soprano is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral composition, usually unaccompanied and polyphonic.

clue.text: Openings in journal regularly taken

indicators.note: letters taken regularly are picked at even intervals, every other one

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Job vacancies listed in a periodical every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: Ora is the Latin plural of os, a mouth or bodily opening, used in anatomy.

clue.text: Drunk and terribly irate learned types

indicators.note: terribly means badly done, so the next word is put in disorder

blocks.note: lit is slang for drunk
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Intellectuals who are drunk and furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read, educated people interested in literature, the intelligentsia.

clue.text: Formal protest organised from Roman centres

indicators.note: organised means arranged into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An official complaint set up by people in Rome's middle districts.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstrance is a forceful, often documented objection, like the Grand Remonstrance put to Charles I.
